name: a-packed-unorm-pair-picks-the-row-the-shader-reads
rationale:
venueWallShadow_vertex packs a vertex attribute into a normalized 16-bit pair, takes the low half as an index, and reads two arrays with it. The index is the whole case: the observed varying is the float4 the shader read at that index, so a packing that lands one row away returns a completely different colour rather than a slightly different number. Nothing here is approximate -- air.pack.unorm2x16.v2f32 is round(saturate(x) * 65535), an integer, and the value it produces is used as an integer.

Eight triangles, one per pixel of an 8x1 target, each carrying the same attribute at all three of its vertices so the interpolated varying is exact and no answer depends on a barycentric weight. Each triangle's base is a fifth of a pixel wide and narrows to a point, so at the row of pixel centres it covers its own centre and comes nowhere near its neighbours'. The eight attributes are chosen at (k - 0.4)/65535: multiplying by 65535 lands four tenths below a whole number, so ROUNDING reaches k and TRUNCATING reaches k-1, and every one of the eight would read the wrong row if the round were dropped. The indices run 1 through 7 and then 15, which is the last row of the sixteen, so an off-by-one at the top of the array shows up as well as one at the bottom. The sixteen colours are distinct and exactly representable, so no row can be mistaken for another.

The rest of the shader is arranged to stay out of the way. Every direction entry is zero, so the unpacked second attribute multiplies to nothing and the clip position is the position attribute unchanged; the view matrix is the identity, so the three column loads and the two multiply-adds reproduce it exactly rather than transforming it. That leaves the packed index as the only thing the observation can be reading.

name: custom-filter-passthrough-zero-state-variant
rationale: A zero shader-state vector disables every optional texture, table, framebuffer-fetch, and dithering branch. The separately linked visible callback returns its incoming half4 unchanged, while zeroed mandatory globals and custom arguments keep every reachable access in bounds. The poisoned one-pixel half4 render target observes the exact linked fragment result.

name: five-index-positions-of-eight-threads-three-wide
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-destination case of this entry, whose zero destination extent returns at the bounds check. Eight threads of one threadgroup each take index position x = thread; the destination extent is 5 (dstSize 5, 1, 1, 1), so threads 5 to 7 return and threads 0 to 4 each read one 4-bit index (fallback offset 2, stride 1: nibble 2 + x of inputPtr) and write the vector LUT's 3 elements (lut0Size 3, 16, 2, 1) to destination elements 3x to 3x + 2 (vector axis 0). Every retained prefixSecondary_f module, the LUT read, returns +0.0, and this entry checks no LUT bound, so elements 0 to 14 hold +0.0 and 15 to 23 keep the 0xab fill: the 24 observed words show the destination bound and the vector-axis coordinates. Each element is written by one thread. The only loop runs the LUT width 3.

name: linked-zero-destination-vector-lut-dequantize-4bit-unaligned
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A single invocation computes coordinate zero while the authored destination extent is zero in every dimension. The top-level destination bounds guard returns before any source, LUT, destination, loop, or linked-function access, leaving the sole poisoned output unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: reset-specular-indirect-count
rationale: The loop-free entry ignores its grid index and unconditionally replaces the complete poisoned four-byte indirect-specular entry counter with aligned i32 zero.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-float-16-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry, whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (offset 0, 64 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[k][n] (row stride w_ld = 16 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in float and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the float inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-float-16-non-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The non-transposed counterpart of the committed qmm_t_16_float case: qmm_n_16_float with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links three translation units, each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule and the matmul2d lowering. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: vertex-float2-position-with-buffer-depth
rationale: Three authored float2 positions form a full-coverage triangle; constant buffer slot 1 supplies finite clip-space depth 0.25, and the typed position observer captures the structural expansion to (x, y, depth, 1).

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert. The authored threadgroup allocation bounds the combined-radix scratch footprint.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seven-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 7 and receives exact float4 zero from all six linked _uber_clear bodies. A nine-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-two-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 22 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-one linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-four-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-five-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 5 and receives exact float4 zero from all four linked _uber_clear bodies. A seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: bicubic-16-bit-normalized-sums-near-the-rounding-tie
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic on 16-bit normalized sums designed near the rounding tie, to pin the 2D datapath (which axis is summed first and where intermediate sums are truncated). Lane i (of 128) reads its own 4x4 block of 64x32 textures (block (i mod 16, i div 16), base texel at the block's (1, 1)) at a seeded random fraction in 1..255 on each axis. Per channel, the block holds: slot 0 (rgba16_unorm) and slot 1 (rgba16_snorm) one nonzero tap, cycling over the 16 positions; slot 2 (rgba16_unorm) two nonzero taps in one row (red, green) or one column (blue, alpha); slots 3 (rgba16_unorm) and 4 (rgba16_snorm) sixteen random codes. The last code placed is the one whose exact sum, in code units, lies nearest a seeded target distance from the half-up tie: log-uniform in 2^-14..2^-3 of a code, either side, one in eight an exact tie (the weights are Metal's measured table). The 1D slots 12 (rgba16_unorm) and 13 (rgba16_snorm) hold 64 texels whose pairs 4a+1, 4a+2 put most of their lanes' bilinear sums near a tie. The other slots bind a 1x1 zero rgba8_unorm texture. Lane i writes its sixteen samples to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-8-bit-normalized-and-srgb-sums-near-the-rounding-tie
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic on 8-bit normalized and sRGB sums designed near the rounding tie, to pin whether the sum is exact before its one rounding. Lanes and blocks as in bicubic-16-bit-normalized-sums-near-the-rounding-tie (128 lanes, own 4x4 block of 64x32 textures, seeded random fractions). Slots: 0 rgba8_unorm one nonzero tap; 1 rgba8_unorm two taps in a row (red, green) or a column (blue, alpha); 2 rgba8_unorm and 3 rgba8_snorm sixteen random codes; 4, 5, 6 rgba8_unorm_srgb one tap, sixteen, and two; 7 rgba8_snorm one tap. The last code placed puts the exact sum nearest a seeded target distance from the half-up tie of the format's measured grid (1/16 of a code; for sRGB colour, 1/4095 after the 12-bit decode round(4095 srgb_to_linear(c/255))): log-uniform in 2^-18..2^-4 of a grid step, either side, one in eight an exact tie. The 1D slots 12 (rgba8_unorm), 13 (rgba8_unorm_srgb) and 14 (rgba8_snorm) hold 64 texels whose pairs 4a+1, 4a+2 put most of their lanes' bilinear sums near a tie. The other slots bind a 1x1 zero rgba8_unorm texture. Lane i writes its sixteen samples to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-accumulator-held-out-half-float-vertical-cancellation-at-x-fraction-0
rationale: Held-out evidence for the unit-weight rule of the half-float Catmull-Rom accumulator model, generated without reference to the model's fit: Metal's bicubic filter (bcx_rules: one clamp-to-edge bicubic sampler with pixel coordinates) on twelve 32x32 half-float 2D textures (rgba16_float, and r16_float and rg16_float among the half-result slots 8-11) at an x fraction of exactly 0, so only the footprint's second column weighs. Lane i (of 256) samples column i mod 32 at a random y fraction over rows 4 (i div 32) to 4 (i div 32) + 3, which hold, per texture and channel, a value A of a random exponent, the half nearest the value cancelling A under the lane's y weights in another row, and small values 2^-d A or zero in the other two. The four 1D slots (12-15) read random half texels at the same x. Lane i writes its sixteen results, the half ones widened to float, to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-accumulator-held-out-random-r-rg-and-rgba-16-and-32-bit-float-in-1d-and-2d
rationale: Held-out evidence for the bicubic accumulator models, generated without reference to them: Metal's bicubic filter (bcx_rules: one clamp-to-edge bicubic sampler with pixel coordinates) over random r16_float, r32_float, rg16_float, rg32_float, rgba16_float, rgba32_float texels. Twelve 16x16 2D textures (slots 0-7 return float, 8-11 half) and four 16-wide 1D ones (12-14 float, 15 half), each channel random across exponents, the negation of its row neighbour (an exact cancellation), a near cancellation of it, a value 2^-d of it, zero, or a multiple of 2^-8 in [-4, 4). Lane i (of 256) samples every texture at its own random pixel coordinate from buffer 0 (the 1D ones at x alone) and writes its sixteen results, the half ones widened to float, to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-accumulator-held-out-random-rgba16-float-in-1d-and-2d
rationale: Held-out evidence for the bicubic accumulator models, generated without reference to them: Metal's bicubic filter (bcx_rules: one clamp-to-edge bicubic sampler with pixel coordinates) over random rgba16_float texels. Twelve 16x16 2D textures (slots 0-7 return float, 8-11 half) and four 16-wide 1D ones (12-14 float, 15 half), each channel random across exponents, the negation of its row neighbour (an exact cancellation), a near cancellation of it, a value 2^-d of it, zero, or a multiple of 2^-8 in [-4, 4). Lane i (of 256) samples every texture at its own random pixel coordinate from buffer 0 (the 1D ones at x alone) and writes its sixteen results, the half ones widened to float, to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-accumulator-held-out-random-rgba32-float-in-1d-and-2d
rationale: Held-out evidence for the bicubic accumulator models, generated without reference to them: Metal's bicubic filter (bcx_rules: one clamp-to-edge bicubic sampler with pixel coordinates) over random rgba32_float texels. Twelve 16x16 2D textures (slots 0-7 return float, 8-11 half) and four 16-wide 1D ones (12-14 float, 15 half), each channel random across exponents, the negation of its row neighbour (an exact cancellation), a near cancellation of it, a value 2^-d of it, zero, or a multiple of 2^-8 in [-4, 4). Lane i (of 256) samples every texture at its own random pixel coordinate from buffer 0 (the 1D ones at x alone) and writes its sixteen results, the half ones widened to float, to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-designed-float-footprints
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic on 2D footprints of designed float texels, each lane reading a 4x4 block of its own (lane i: block (4 (i mod 16), 4 (i div 16)) of 64x32 textures, base texel at the block's (1, 1)) at fractions (128, 128), (64, 192), (1, 255) or (37, 200) by lane mod 4. Slot 0 binds rgba32_float, whose bilinear sum of the inner 2x2 is designed per channel: two large terms that cancel exactly leaving two terms 30 to 100 binades smaller, the same leaving one ulp of a large term, a tie broken by terms 2^-60, subnormal terms, random exponents within 2^±120, three-way cancellation, ties on a coarse grid, and infinite outer taps the bilinear filter does not read. Slot 1 binds rgba16_float with random halves over every binade, halves below 2^-6, an outer ring of -65504 around an inner 65504 (overshoot), mixed magnitudes with cancelling large taps, and multiples of 2^-24. Slots 8 and 9 read the same two textures as half; every other slot binds a 1x1 zero rgba8_unorm texture. Lane i writes its sixteen samples to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-designed-ties-clamps-and-extremes
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic on designed sums: ties of each format's rounding, clamps past -1 and 1, the most negative signed code, half overflow and its rounding boundary, subnormal sums, non-finite texels on weighted and zero-weight taps, and exact sums across binades. Each 16x16 texture holds 64 four-tap patterns per channel: row r, columns 4g..4g+3 are the taps of base column 4g + 1. Lane 4p + j (p = 4r + g) samples pixel coordinate (4g + 1.5 + k/256, r + 0.5) for k in (0, 64, 128, 192): vertical fraction 0, so one row is read, with the Catmull-Rom weights of k/256 (exact at 0 and 128) or the bilinear weights of the 32-bit float formats. Slots: rgba16_snorm, rgba8_snorm, rgba16_unorm, rgba8_unorm, rgba16_float, rgba32_float, rg16_snorm, rgba16_unorm; the half slots read the rgba16_float, rgba32_float, rgba16_snorm and rgba8_snorm textures; the 1D slots hold row 0's taps of the rgba16_snorm, rgba8_snorm and rgba32_float textures and the rgba16_float one read as half. Lane i writes its sixteen samples to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-filter-accumulator-of-rgba16-float-in-1d-and-2d
rationale: How Metal's bicubic filter accumulates rgba16_float texels in 1D and 2D (Catmull-Rom over the 4x4 under Metal's weight table in 2D, bilinear over taps i and i + 1 in 1D), with float and half results: eight 32x32 2D textures in the float slots, the first four again in the half slots, three 16-wide 1D textures in the 1D float slots and the first again in the 1D half slot. The 2D values are 64 4x4 blocks sharing each block's x fraction across the textures: per channel, two values in one row scaled to cancel exactly under the block's x weights beside two smaller values with full significands; a value whose weighted term at y fraction 128 is an exact half tie beside a much smaller value; or, in blocks sampled at a texel centre in x, huge values in the columns of weight zero beside smaller ones. The 1D values are eight pairs: a value whose weighted term is an exact tie at the pair's designed fraction, beside a much smaller value of either sign. Lane i reads a pixel coordinate from buffer 0: for i < 128 a 2D block's footprint at its x fraction and y fraction 128 or another, for i >= 128 a 1D pair at its designed fraction or another one. Every texture is sampled at the coordinate (the 1D ones at x alone) through one bicubic clamp-to-edge sampler with pixel coordinates; lane i writes its sixteen results, the half ones widened to float, to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-filter-accumulator-of-rgba32-float-in-1d-and-2d
rationale: How Metal's bicubic filter accumulates rgba32_float texels in 1D and 2D (bilinear over the inner 2x2 in 2D, over taps i and i + 1 in 1D), with float and half results: eight 16x16 2D textures in the float slots, the first four again in the half slots, three 16-wide 1D textures in the 1D float slots and the first again in the 1D half slot. The 2D values are 64 2x2 blocks sharing each block's x fraction across the textures: per channel, a row (or column) of a value and its negation scaled to cancel exactly at the block's x fraction beside two smaller values with full significands; a value whose weighted term is an exact f32 tie beside a much smaller value; or, in blocks sampled at a texel centre in x, huge values in the column of weight zero beside smaller ones. The 1D values are eight pairs: a value whose weighted term is an exact tie at the pair's designed fraction, beside a much smaller value of either sign. Lane i reads a pixel coordinate from buffer 0: for i < 128 a 2D block at its x fraction and one of six y fractions, for i >= 128 a 1D pair at its designed fraction or another one. Every texture is sampled at the coordinate (the 1D ones at x alone) through one bicubic clamp-to-edge sampler with pixel coordinates; lane i writes its sixteen results, the half ones widened to float, to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-float-cancellation-ties-and-non-finite-texels
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic on designed float sums: how much of a sum survives cancellation, how a tie is broken by a small term, and how non-finite texels propagate. Lane i (of 64) reads its own 4x4 block of 64x16 textures (block (i mod 16, i div 16), base texel at the block's (1, 1)) at fraction (128, 128), (64, 192), seeded random, or (0, 128) by i mod 4. Per channel: slots 0 (rgba16_float, Catmull-Rom) and 3 (rgba32_float, bilinear over the inner 2x2) hold two taps of equal weight at A and -A (A a random value of a random binade) and a residual 0..30 (half) or 0..80 (float) binades below A by rung, with an opposite-signed second residual three binades lower on odd rungs; slots 1 (rgba16_float) and 4 (rgba32_float) hold a sum exactly half an ulp of the result format above a representable value, plus or minus 2^-n ulp (n = 1..40 by rung) or nothing; slots 2 (rgba16_float) and 5 (rgba32_float) hold finite texels in [-4, 4] with +inf, -inf or NaN at one tap cycling over the 16 positions, or two (inf and -inf, inf and NaN, two infs, -inf and NaN, two NaNs) at diagonally opposite taps, at weighted and zero-weight taps alike. Slot 8 reads slot 3's texture as half. The 1D slots hold 64 texels: 12 (rgba16_float) and 13 (rgba32_float) a value and the texel that cancels it under the lane's bilinear weights down to a residual, 14 (rgba32_float) non-finite texels at the read pair and outside it, 15 (rgba32_float, read as half) ladders like 13. Slots 6, 7, 9-11 bind a 1x1 zero rgba8_unorm texture. Lane i writes its sixteen samples to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

creation_bound.measured: On an RTX 3090 with NVIDIA 615.71.09 the driver compiles this kernel's module (122,640 bytes of SPIR-V) in 1.4 s of its thread's CPU time on an idle host (1,405 ms, 1,414 ms of wall time), and in more of it as other work shares the host's 8 cores and 16 threads: 2.6 to 4.1 s at a load of 15 to 19, with at most 0.4 ms of waits for a CPU, and 4.3 to 5.3 s beside 32 spinning threads (a load of 29 to 50), where the creation clock read 4.35 s once 8.2 s of waits for a CPU were left out. An RTX 5080 Laptop GPU with the same driver compiles it in about 1.0 s at a load of 12 to 15.

name: bicubic-rounding-of-random-float-and-srgb-texels
rationale: How Metal's filter::bicubic sums and rounds float and sRGB texels, read from random texels: slots 0-7 bind 16x16 textures of r16_float and rgba16_float (random finite halves over every binade, subnormals included), rgba32_float (random binary32 values with exponents in [-30, 30]), rg16_float (random halves), rgba8_unorm_srgb (random codes), rgba16_float (halves below 2^-6, many subnormal), r32_float (exponents in [-8, 8]) and rgba32_float (multiples of 2^-8 in [-4, 4), a quarter offset by a multiple of 2^-24, so sums tie); the half slots 8-11 bind the textures of slots 1, 2, 4 and 7 again, read as half; the 1D slots 12-15 bind 16-texel rgba16_float, rgba32_float and rgba8_unorm_srgb textures and an rgba32_float one read as half. Lanes as in bicubic-rounding-of-random-normalized-texels (256 lanes, each axis every 1/256 fraction once, seeded bases). Lane i writes its sixteen samples to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-rounding-of-random-normalized-texels
rationale: How Metal's filter::bicubic rounds the sums of normalized formats, read from random texels: slots 0-7 bind 16x16 textures of r16_unorm, rgba16_unorm, r16_snorm, rg16_snorm, rgba16_snorm, r8_snorm, rgba8_snorm and rgba8_unorm holding uniformly random codes over the format's whole range (the most negative signed code included); the half slots 8-11 bind the textures of slots 1, 4, 6 and 7 again, read as half; the 1D slots 12-15 bind 16-texel rgba16_unorm, rgba8_unorm and rgba16_snorm textures and an rgba8_snorm one read as half, random likewise. Lane i (of 256) samples pixel coordinate (bx + 0.5 + i/256, by + 0.5 + ((167 i + 59) mod 256)/256) with seeded random base texels, so each axis takes every 1/256 fraction once, through one clamp-to-edge bicubic sampler with pixel coordinates (the 1D slots at its x). Lane i writes its sixteen samples to out[16i..16i+15] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: widen-a-range-by-three-and-a-half-without-contracting
rationale: The module is compiled air.compile.fast_math_disable, so its `avg + d*3.5` and `avg - d*3.5` are a separate multiply and add that Metal must not fuse. An average above the maximum makes the half-extent negative, which is what keeps the two fmin/fmax clamps from masking either result, and the very low minimum keeps the other clamp open. The three inputs are chosen so that the rounded product differs from the exact one and both the widened lower and upper bound land on a different float when the pair is contracted into an fma, so the observed 68 bytes distinguish contraction from its absence.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-four-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 24 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-three linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: execute-two-gpu-encoded-template-dispatches
rationale: Two threads each encode one compute command and write nothing else, so only executing the commands observes them. Command t takes the template icb_replay_template from the argument buffer's pipeline-state member (token 1, the template's own case), binds the params window and the out window at 256 * t bytes as kernel buffers 0 and 1, sets a 32-byte threadgroup length, dispatches 64 threads in groups of 8 (command 0 as 8 threadgroups, command 1 as 64 threads), and sets a barrier. After the producer, the execution runs both commands with no inherited state: window 0's params are scale 3 and bias 5, window 1's scale 7 and bias 11, so out holds 3 * t + 8 for t in 0..64, then 7 * t + 18. Every selected byte differs from the 0xab fill.

name: constant-half4-white
rationale: The fragment entry ignores its stage inputs and returns literal half4 (1,1,1,1) at color location zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned pixel.

name: a-64-bit-index-multiply-add-read-through-its-low-word
rationale: Eight threads read in[ulong(t) * 3 + 1]: the compiler keeps the index as an i64 multiply and add whose only use is the load's getelementptr, which the engine holds as its low word (arith.index_word). in[k] = 0x1000 + k over 24 words, so out[t] = 0x1000 + 3t + 1 = (4097, 4100, 4103, 4106, 4109, 4112, 4115, 4118). The AIR has no loop.

name: resample-one-texel-centre-from-the-second-source-layer
rationale: A 2x4 dispatch; the observed texel is the invocation at tid (1, 3, 0). destinationSize is (2, 4, 1), so no lane of the `any(destinationSize <= tid)` guard fires for any invocation and all eight run. air.convert.f.v3f32.u.v3i16 turns that tid into (1.0, 3.0, 0.0) -- the two non-zero lanes differ, so a conversion that swaps lanes, narrows, or drops one moves the sample. scaleFactor is (1/8, 1/8), so the coordinate is (1/8 + 1/2, 3/8 + 1/2) = (0.625, 0.875), and on a four-wide four-tall source those are exactly the centres of texels 2 and 3: every term is a dyadic rational, so the multiply-add is exact and the sample is unambiguous for any filter. The sampler is authored nearest anyway. sourceOrigin is (0, 0, 1), so the signed conversion feeding the layer picks source layer 1, and air.convert.u.i32.f.f32 truncates 1.0 to slice 1. The 32 source texels are all distinct, so landing on the wrong texel, the wrong layer, or the wrong destination texel changes the bytes; the answer is source layer 1 texel (2, 3), which is (132, 132.25, 132.5, 132.75). What this case cannot separate is unsigned from signed on the tid conversion, because a thread position is never negative.

name: dot-of-two-to-four-float-and-half-lanes-under-fast-math
rationale: Thread i reads the float vectors x and y from in[2i] and in[2i + 1] and writes 8 words: dot(x.xy, y.xy), dot(x.xyz, y.xyz), dot(x, y); the same three on half(x) and half(y), each a half's bits in a word; and, with a = x.x, b = x.y, c = x.z, dot(float2(a, b), float2(b, c)) and dot(float2(a, b), float2(b, a)). Over the 512 lanes: twelve lanes where only Metal's fused chain fma(x[n-1], y[n-1], ... fma(x[1], y[1], x[0] * y[0])) gives all three float or half words (no other order, tree, unfused or exact sum does), every (a, b, c) of signed zeros, ones and the smallest normals in about half the cases, denormal operands of both signs, and near-cancellations of every lane, with no lane whose chain meets the tininess edge before rounding. It measures how Metal sums dot and its zero signs. Compiled under the default fast math, every call carrying every fast-math flag.

name: integer-median3-words
rationale: Every air.median3 form Metal's compiler emits from MSL's integer median3, in one loop-free kernel: s and u of i8, i16, i32 and i64, s.v4i8, u.v2i16, and s and u of v4i32 and v2i64. Each of the 64 threads (two threadgroups of 32) reads three 64-bit words and writes 32 words: each scalar type's median of the words cast to it (a narrow signed one sign-extended), then the vectors' lanes, each over other operands (the words' four low bytes, two low halves, low and high halves and those of their complements, the words and their complements). For each width the words hold the six orders of its INT_MIN, INT_MAX and all ones (-1, UINT_MAX), where the signed and unsigned medians differ; four ties of them and all three alike; zeros, all ones and 0/1 mixes; and 20 threads of splitmix64 words.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nt-half-k40-two-experts
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-shape case of this entry, whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 64 lanes (2 simdgroups) runs the single 16x64 output tile: B = 1, M = 16, N = 64, K = 40 (gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2, remainder 8), no dimension declared aligned (user constant 0): the remainder and both whole blocks go through the guarded loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (experts_stride_b = N*K = 2560), writing only its own rows. B[e][n][k] (ldb = 40): expert 0 holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the 64 column sums differ, and expert 1 holds q/2. A[m][k] (lda = 40): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating along k, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . q/2 = a . q): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (256 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Every input is a multiple of 0.5 at most 15, exact in half; every product is a multiple of 0.5 at most 75 and every sum of 40 at most 3000, below 2^12: exact in float in any order or contraction. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the row-segment scan stops at M = 16, the K loop runs gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2 times, the segment loop ends after the two segments, and the element loops have constant trip counts.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nt-half-zero-shape
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The nt half counterpart of the committed mps_gather_mm_rhs_nn_half case: mps_gather_mm_rhs_nt_half with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible function (postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule and the matmul2d lowering. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eight-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 8 and receives exact float4 zero from all seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A ten-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

name: blit-through-a-uniform-rasterization-rate-map
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.map_screen_to_physical_coordinates.v2f32.p2i8.i32 (34 case-less sources), through a rasterization-rate map whose rate is a uniform 1.0: a 64x64 screen, one layer, one horizontal and one vertical sample of 1.0, so physical coordinates equal screen coordinates in both implementations. Buffer 0 is authored as that map: the Metal oracle compiles it with newRasterizationRateMapWithDescriptor: and binds the data copyParameterDataToBuffer:offset: writes, and a Vulkan executor binds the product's parameter data of the same map (bind::RasterizationRateMap), which the engine's decoder reads; the old engine lowers the call to the identity and reads neither. The static sampler is pixel-coordinate ClampToEdge LINEAR, so sampling at float2(gid) puts the filter weight at exactly one half on every axis, and the source texel (x, y, x+y, 1) makes every blend a half-integer that is exact in binary32. The offset buffer is zero, so the destination coordinate is the thread id and a mapping that scaled or shifted the sample coordinate would move every texel. Replaces b50a20ca, which carried Apple's parameter bytes of the same map (private to Apple's implementation, so not the product's map).

name: put-the-ninetieth-percentile-exactly-on-a-bin-edge
rationale: A 90th-percentile search whose two-stage scan is built from air.simd_prefix_inclusive_sum.u.i32: each of the eight simdgroups scans its own 32 histogram bins, then simdgroup 0 walks the seven block boundaries in lockstep to turn the per-simdgroup scans into one 256-bin prefix sum. One 256-thread threadgroup makes threads_per_simdgroup=32 and simdgroups_per_threadgroup=8, so every stride loop runs exactly once and all three threadgroup barriers stay convergent. linearSystemStatus=0 takes the working path instead of the early store of zero. The counts are chosen so the whole float tail is exact rather than merely close: the total is 2^23, the only total for which 0.9f times it is an integer (0.9f = 15099494*2^-24, so the product needs 2^23 to clear the odd factor), giving a threshold of exactly 7549747. Bins 100 and 200 hold 6710886 and 1677722, so the prefix crosses the threshold first at bin 200 with 6710886 below and 8388608 at it -- and (7549747-6710886)/(8388608-6710886) is exactly 1/2. At t=0.5 Metal's mix(x,y,a)=x+(y-x)a and GLSL's FMix=x(1-a)+ya agree bit-for-bit, so the case does not silently depend on which formula the lowering picks, and the fdiv is exact under a reciprocal-multiply as well. The result collapses to bin/32 = 6.25.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-six-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 6 and receives exact float4 zero from all five linked _uber_clear bodies. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: constant-half4-render-target
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns a constant half4 to attachment zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned RGBA16Float pixel.
